gloss: to hand down (a sentence); to pronounce; to order

definitions.gloss: to hand down; to pronounce; to pass (a sentence)
definitions.explanation: To officially announce a verdict, judgment, or decision, typically in legal or formal contexts.
To give an official order or directive to someone.

examples.japanese: {判決|はんけつ}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}す。
{裁判官|さいばんかん}が{被告|ひこく}に{有罪|ゆうざい}{判決|はんけつ}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}した。
examples.english: The judge handed down a guilty verdict to the defendant.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}から{余命|よめい}{半年|はんとし}と{言|い}い{渡|わた}された。
examples.english: The doctor told me I have six months to live.

examples.japanese: {上司|じょうし}から{転勤|てんきん}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}された。
examples.english: I was ordered by my boss to transfer.

examples.japanese: {社長|しゃちょう}から{退職|たいしょく}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}された。
examples.english: The president ordered me to resign.

examples.japanese: {学校|がっこう}から{一週間|いっしゅうかん}の{停学|ていがく}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}された。
examples.english: I was given a one-week suspension by the school.

notes:
CONJUGATION:
・{言|い}い{渡|わた}す → {言|い}い{渡|わた}さない (negative)
・{言|い}い{渡|わた}す → {言|い}い{渡|わた}して (te-form)
・{言|い}い{渡|わた}す → {言|い}い{渡|わた}した (past)

FORMATION:
Compound verb: {言|い}う (to say) + {渡|わた}す (to hand over)

The combination conveys officially delivering words/decisions.

COLLOCATIONS:
・{判決|はんけつ}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}す - to hand down a verdict
・{刑|けい}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}す - to pronounce a sentence
・{解雇|かいこ}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}す - to deliver notice of dismissal
・{余命|よめい}を{言|い}い{渡|わた}す - to tell someone their life expectancy

REGISTER:
Formal/written style. Common in legal and official contexts.
